newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Most metals prices seen rising - Macquarie Equities.
newsitem.headline: Most metals prices seen rising - Macquarie Equities.

text.p: A current dip in metals commodities prices will be short-lived, with stronger economic growth leading to increased demand and boosting prices, Australia-based Macquarie Equities Ltd forecast in a report on Tuesday.
The preferred commodites are zinc, nickel and aluminium due to forecast deficits in supply this year and in 1998, it said.
A key exception is copper, where Macquarie sees a tight supply and demand ratio, resulting in prices remaining volatile due to low stock levels, Macquarie said.
"Growth in copper production will drive the market into surplus in 1997 and 1998," Macquarie said, adding the copper price should retreat to around US$1.00 a pound.
Spot copper currently fetches about US$1.10 a pound.
However, currently, total stocks of copper remain "extremely low" and should hold at below five weeks of consumption until the end of 1999, the bank said.
"The continuing low level of stocks leaves the market vulnerable to intermittent periods of tightness and prices are likely to remain extremely volatile," Macquarie said.
This situation has been exacerbated by an on-going technical squeeze in the market, it said.

The backwardation in cash-to-three-months copper at the London Metal Exchange increased by about US$100 a tonne on Monday to around US$250 a tonne as investors scrambled for metal to deliver to meet July market obligations.
